summary: Winema-area Aermotor tower on Applegate Butte, built 1935-36 for the Klamath Indian Agency, abandoned as a lookout and removed in 2016; the site is now a communications site.

facts.design: 80-foot steel Aermotor LS-40 tower with a cabin
facts.status_note: Tower dismantled and removed in 2016; the site is now used for communications
facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service; built for the Klamath Indian Agency and run by the Oregon Department of Forestry from 1961

events.note: Built by a CCC-ID crew for the Klamath Indian Agency, per the Forest Lookouts (Oregon) history; its buildings were completed by May 31. Register and FFLOS give 1936.
Named lookout Norman Doty quit in August 1949
Responsibility passed to the Oregon Department of Forestry under the termination act
Radio shack announced in a May 7, 1963 Herald and News item as to be built near the lookout; completion not confirmed
Repairs to a concrete foundation block; new deck on the cabin porch
Tower dismantled and removed in early winter 2016; living quarters destroyed
Site taken over by the Oregon Department of Transportation for a communications tower

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Most sources give 80 feet, including the Klamath agency records and the FFLOS record. firelookout.com gives 100 feet, and a 1967 survey recovery note quoted on the Forest Lookouts (Oregon) page gives 90 feet. The record's 24.4 m (80 ft) is kept.
The register gives 6,040 ft (1,841 m); the FFLOS and firelookout.com give 6,079 ft (1,853 m). The record keeps the register figure.

notes_for_editor: Build year is unresolved: register and FFLOS give 1936, while the Klamath agency entry on the Forest Lookouts (Oregon) page describes a 1935 build. Both are given; events carry 1935 with the 1936 note. The 2016 ODOT claim is only on the Forest Lookouts (Oregon) page and was not checked with ODOT. The FS project page is marked cancelled; its milestones give a 01/06/2012 scoping start and estimated 2014 decision and implementation dates, and it was last updated 2/26/2014. Public access and the current condition of any structure at the site are not described by any source read. FFLOS photo credits (Rex Kamstra, Ron Kemnow, Howard Verschoor collection) were not added because no licence was given. Page reads: seven, one over the brief's six, because the Oregon Lookouts page had to be read three times to reach its later entries.
